name: GALLIUM
affiliation_detail:
GALLIUM is widely assessed as a Chinese state-sponsored group. Microsoft identified the group based on tools and TTPs "commonly associated with Chinese threat actors" and noted that its C2 infrastructure was hosted on servers in mainland China, Hong Kong SAR, and Taiwan. (MSTIC, 2019)
Cybereason initially attributed GALLIUM's telecom targeting campaign to activity consistent with APT10, though Microsoft subsequently tracked it under the separate GALLIUM designation. (Cybereason, 2019; MSTIC, 2019)
No specific MSS bureau, PLA unit, or contractor has been publicly named. No individuals have been indicted. The relationship between GALLIUM and APT10 remains ambiguous — Cybereason noted TTPs consistent with APT10, while Microsoft tracks GALLIUM as a separate entity.
description:
GALLIUM is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group that has been active since at least 2012, specializing in the compromise of telecommunications infrastructure to enable large-scale surveillance. The group was first publicly exposed by Cybereason in June 2019 under the campaign name "Operation Soft Cell," and subsequently designated GALLIUM by Microsoft in December 2019. (Cybereason, 2019; MSTIC, 2019)
Operation Soft Cell involved multi-year intrusions into global telecommunications providers to steal Call Detail Records (CDRs) — metadata containing the communications, geolocation, and associations of specific high-value individuals. (Cybereason, 2019) At least a dozen global telecommunications providers were affected.
Beginning in 2021, Unit 42 documented an expansion of GALLIUM's targeting beyond telecoms to include financial institutions and government entities across nine countries, accompanied by the deployment of a new RAT called PingPull. (Unit 42, 2022) In 2023, Unit 42 identified a Linux variant of PingPull and a previously undocumented backdoor called Sword2033, deployed against targets in South Africa. (Unit 42, 2023)  In 2024, Unit 42 reported intrusions  directed at SEA governments attributed to Alloy Taurus. (Unit 42, 2024)
ESET's 2024 reporting identified GALLIUM activity using SoftEther VPN across African telecom operators. (ESET, 2024)

campaigns.name: Operation Soft Cell
campaigns.description: Cybereason exposed a sustained campaign active since at least 2012 targeting global telecommunications providers. The attackers compromised carrier networks to steal Call Detail Records, enabling surveillance of specific high-value individuals' communications, geolocation, and associations. The group achieved total network compromise, exfiltrating "hundreds of gigabytes of call data records" each time.

campaigns.name: DeadRinger (Telecom Intrusions Continuation)
campaigns.description: Cybereason documented three concurrent clusters of Chinese APT activity targeting Southeast Asian telecoms, including continued Soft Cell operations through Q1 2021. The group exploited Microsoft Exchange ProxyLogon vulnerabilities, deploying PcShare backdoor and China Chopper web shells to access CDRs and billing systems.

sources.title: DeadRinger: Exposing Chinese Threat Actors Targeting Major Telcos

campaigns.name: PingPull Multi-Sector Expansion
campaigns.description: Unit 42 identified GALLIUM expanding beyond telecoms to target financial institutions and government entities across nine countries: Afghanistan, Australia, Belgium, Cambodia, Malaysia, Mozambique, the Philippines, Russia, and Vietnam. The group deployed a new RAT called PingPull using ICMP, HTTPS, and raw TCP for C2 communications. Over 170 IP addresses were mapped in GALLIUM's infrastructure. (Unit 42, 2022)

campaigns.name: Southeast Asian Government Espionage
campaigns.description: Unit 42 attributed with moderate confidence a multiwave intrusion campaign against a Southeast Asian government from 2022 through 2023 to Alloy Taurus. The group exploited Exchange Server vulnerabilities, deployed China Chopper web shells, and used renamed SoftEther VPN for persistence — a combination unique to GALLIUM operations.
